# Introduction

COVID-19 spreads between basic health areas (ABS) as well as within them. The endemic-epidemic model `hhh4`
[@meyer2014; @meyer2017] splits the cases in each area and time period into three parts:

- **Endemic**: cases not linked to recent cases, in proportion to population.
- **Autoregressive**: cases from past cases in the same ABS.
- **Neighbour**: cases from past cases in other ABS.

The neighbour component needs weights that define which ABS are linked and how closely. Standard models base these
weights on shared borders. People often travel beyond adjacent areas, so trips may describe contact between ABS
better. We test this on weekly cases in Catalunya's 374 ABS from 22 March 2020 to 1 May 2021, with neighbours
defined by shared boundaries, by trip orders or by trip shares. We compare the three by in-sample fit, one-week-ahead
forecasts and how the fitted cases split across the components, and check whether the ranking holds with
temperature and restrictions. We also check whether people's destinations changed with the restrictions, and how
they differ between urban and rural ABS.

The data combine five sources:

- **Cases**: confirmed COVID-19 counts from BSC Flow-Maps [@poncedeleon2024data], with two ABS taken from the
  official CatSalut series.
- **Mobility**: daily trips between ABS from MITMA [@niraula2026data].
- **Population**: the 2021 registered population of each ABS (CatSalut).
- **Temperature**: daily mean temperature by ABS (AEMET).
- **Restrictions**: the dates of the national and Catalan decrees (BOE, DOGC).

# Data

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: libraries
suppressMessages({
	library(surveillance)
	library(sf)
	library(ggplot2)
	library(dplyr)
	library(tidyr)
	library(patchwork)
})

# Input folders: the Catalunya panel (Spain-data) and the derived inputs of
# bayesian-end-epi-mobility; set SPAIN_DATA and INPUTS to use other locations
spain = \(...) file.path(Sys.getenv("SPAIN_DATA", "../Spain-data"), ...)
out = \(f) file.path(Sys.getenv("INPUTS", "../slater/outputs"), f)

# Plot theme and colours
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
	theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))
LONLAT = coord_sf(datum = st_crs(4326))
COMPONENT = c(Endemic = "grey70", Autoregressive = "#3b6ea8",
	Neighbour = "#e0913a")
MODEL = c(Boundaries = "#3b6ea8", `Trip orders` = "#e0913a",
	`Trip shares` = "#6a9f58")
ORDER = c(Origin = "black", `1` = "#c6dbef", `2` = "#6baed6",
	`3` = "#2171b5")
```

```{r}
#| label: helpers
# Fitted cases of each component, [week, ABS]
components = \(f) {
	m = meanHHH(f$coefficients, terms(f))
	list(Endemic = m$endemic, Autoregressive = m$epi.own,
		Neighbour = m$epi.neighbours, mean = m$mean)
}

# Get model diagnostics
diagnostics = \(f) {
	y = observed(f$stsObj)[f$control$subset, ]
	c(AIC = AIC(f), logLik = as.numeric(logLik(f)),
		RMSE = sqrt(mean((y - fitted(f))^2)))
}

# Estimate and 95% Wald interval, computed on the scale of estimation: log for
# the rates and ratios in exp_names, log(1 / psi) for the overdispersion
wald = \(f, exp_names) {
	b = coef(f, reparamPsi = FALSE)
	se = sqrt(diag(vcov(f, reparamPsi = FALSE)))
	x = cbind(est = b, lo = b - 1.96 * se, hi = b + 1.96 * se)
	e = names(b) %in% exp_names
	x[e, ] = exp(x[e, ])
	o = names(b) == "-log(overdisp)"
	x[o, ] = exp(-x[o, c(1, 3, 2)])
	rownames(x)[o] = "overdisp"
	x
}

# Components of one fit as a long table, for the ABS in cols
long = \(m, cols = seq_len(n)) names(COMPONENT) |>
	lapply(\(p) data.frame(component = p,
		date = rep(dates[-1], length(cols)),
		abs = rep(abs$name[cols], each = length(dates) - 1),
		cases = c(m[[p]][, cols, drop = FALSE]))) |>
	bind_rows() |>
	mutate(component = factor(component, rev(names(COMPONENT))))
```

## Load and process data

```{r}
#| label: data
# Daily cases and population, 22 March 2020 to 1 May 2021
d = readRDS(out("daily_catalunya_2020-03-22_2021-05-01_inputs.rds"))
ids = d$ids
n = length(ids)
popv = d$pop
stopifnot(n == 374, length(d$dates) == 406,
	weekdays(d$dates[1]) == "Sunday")

# ABS polygons, in the order of the cases
abs = spain("outputs/catalunya/geometry/cat_abs.gpkg") |>
	st_read(quiet = TRUE) |>
	slice(match(ids, id))

# Weekly cases, Sunday to Saturday, [ABS, week]
week = rep(1:58, each = 7)
Y = d$cases |>
	apply(1, \(x) tapply(x, week, sum)) |>
	t()
dates = d$dates[seq(1, 406, 7)]

# Mean trips a day between ABS, [origin, destination]
od = readRDS(out("od_monthly_catalunya_2020-03-22_2021-05-01.rds"))
stopifnot(identical(dimnames(od$trips)[[1]], ids))
trips = apply(od$trips, 1:2, sum) / 406
diag(trips) = 0

# Daily trips out of each ABS, temperature and restrictions, from the panel
panel = spain("outputs/catalunya/panel/cat_abs_main_noncollinear.parquet") |>
	arrow::read_parquet(col_select = c("id", "date", "trips_out", "temp_mean",
		"npi_alarm", "npi_hibernation", "npi_curfew", "npi_hospitality")) |>
	filter(id %in% ids, date >= min(d$dates), date <= max(d$dates)) |>
	mutate(week = week[match(date, d$dates)])
stopifnot(nrow(panel) == n * 406, !anyNA(panel))

# Trips out of all ABS, weekly mean of the daily totals, millions a day
mobility = panel |>
	summarise(trips = sum(trips_out), .by = c(week, date)) |>
	summarise(trips = mean(trips) / 1e6, .by = week) |>
	mutate(date = dates[week])

# Weekly mean of a daily variable, [week, ABS]
weekly = \(v) tapply(panel[[v]], list(panel$week, panel$id), mean)[, ids]

# Adjacency of the ABS (queen), [from, to]
a = readRDS(spain("outputs/catalunya/geometry/cat_abs_topology.rds"))$adjacency
a = a[ids, ids]
diag(a) = 0

# Restrictions in force in Catalunya, with the dates of the decrees
source(spain("helpers/restrictions.R"))
npi = NPI |>
	filter(region %in% c("ES", "CT")) |>
	select(measure, label, start, end)
alarm = filter(npi, measure == "npi_alarm")
stopifnot(nrow(npi) == 5, nrow(alarm) == 2)
```

**Catalunya: `r ncol(Y)` weeks, `r n` ABS, `r format(sum(Y), big.mark = ",")` cases.**

## Exploratory visualization

```{r}
#| label: fig-series
#| fig-cap: "Weekly cases per 100,000 in each ABS and in Catalunya as a whole, with the trips out of all ABS below. Lines mark when each restriction starts (solid) or ends (dashed)."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7
# Colour of each measure
NPI_COL = c(npi_alarm = "#6a3d9a", npi_hibernation = "#1b9e77",
	npi_hospitality = "#d95f02", npi_curfew = "#6a3d9a")

# Day month year, without a leading zero
day = \(x) paste(as.integer(format(x, "%d")), format(x, "%b %Y"))

# Starts and ends inside the study window, one line per date
window = range(dates) + c(0, 6)
events = bind_rows(
		mutate(npi, date = start, type = "start", text = label),
		mutate(npi, date = end, type = "end", text = paste("End:", label))) |>
	filter(date > window[1], date < window[2]) |>
	summarise(text = paste(text, collapse = " and "), measure = measure[1],
		.by = c(date, type)) |>
	mutate(text = paste0(sub(" and Curfew", " and curfew", text), ", ",
		day(date))) |>
	arrange(date) |>
	mutate(text = factor(text, text))

# Starts and ends outside the window, for the caption
outside = bind_rows(mutate(npi, date = start, what = "began"),
		mutate(npi, date = end, what = "ended")) |>
	filter(date < window[1] | date > window[2]) |>
	summarise(text = paste(label, collapse = " and "), .by = c(date, what)) |>
	mutate(text = paste(sub(" and Curfew", " and curfew", text), what,
		day(date)))

# Event lines in one key: colour by measure, solid at starts, dashed at ends
lines = list(
	geom_vline(data = events, aes(xintercept = date, colour = text,
		linetype = text), linewidth = 0.5),
	scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(NPI_COL[events$measure],
		events$text), name = "Restrictions"),
	scale_linetype_manual(values = setNames(ifelse(events$type == "start",
		"solid", "dashed"), events$text), name = "Restrictions"),
	scale_x_date(limits = window, expand = c(0, 0)))

# Weekly cases per 100,000 in Catalunya as a whole: all cases over all residents
regional = data.frame(date = dates, inc = colSums(Y) / sum(popv) * 1e5)

# Weekly incidence by ABS, with Catalunya as a whole
incidence = data.frame(id = rep(ids, 58), date = rep(dates, each = n),
		inc = c(Y) / popv * 1e5) |>
	ggplot(aes(date, inc)) +
	geom_line(aes(group = id, colour = "One ABS"), linewidth = 0.1,
		alpha = 0.3) +
	geom_line(data = regional, aes(colour = "Catalunya"), linewidth = 0.8) +
	scale_colour_manual(values = c(`One ABS` = "#9ecae1",
		Catalunya = "black"), name = "Cases",
		guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1, linewidth = 0.6))) +
	ggnewscale::new_scale_colour() +
	lines +
	scale_y_sqrt() +
	labs(x = NULL, y = "Cases per 100,000\n(square root scale)") +
	theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())

# Trips out of all ABS
trips_plot = mobility |>
	ggplot(aes(date, trips)) +
	lines +
	geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
	geom_point(size = 0.8) +
	labs(x = NULL, y = "Trips out of ABS\n(millions a day)")

# Lowest week of trips, and the range of trips during the two later waves
low = mobility[which.min(mobility$trips), ]
waves = range(filter(mobility, date >= as.Date("2020-09-01"),
	date < as.Date("2021-03-01"))$trips)

# Cases above, trips below, on the same time axis, keys on the side
incidence / trips_plot +
	plot_layout(heights = c(2, 1), guides = "collect") +
	plot_annotation(
		title = "Catalunya: weekly cases by ABS, trips and restrictions",
		caption = paste0("Outside the window: ",
			paste(outside$text, collapse = "; "), "."))
```

Trips fell to `r sprintf("%.1f", low$trips)` million a day in the week of `r day(low$date)`, as cases fell under the
first state of alarm. The autumn and winter waves came while trips stayed between `r sprintf("%.1f", waves[1])` and
`r sprintf("%.1f", waves[2])` million a day: the volume of trips alone does not track the waves. The trip
neighbourhoods test whether where people travel matters instead.

```{r}
#| label: frames
# Weekly cases per 100,000, [week, ABS], in classes up to the highest week
incidence_w = t(Y) / rep(popv, each = 58) * 1e5
CASES_AT = c(0, 50, 100, 200, 400, 800, 13000)
stopifnot(max(incidence_w) < max(CASES_AT))

# One frame: the cases map, and the trips with the week marked
# A weekly series with the restriction lines and the mapped week marked
series = \(x, v, w, label) x |>
	ggplot(aes(date, .data[[v]])) +
	geom_vline(data = events, aes(xintercept = date, colour = measure,
		linetype = type), linewidth = 0.4, show.legend = FALSE) +
	scale_colour_manual(values = NPI_COL) +
	scale_linetype_manual(values = c(start = "solid", end = "dashed")) +
	geom_line(colour = "grey30") +
	geom_point(data = x[w, ], size = 2.5) +
	scale_x_date(limits = window, expand = c(0, 0)) +
	labs(x = NULL, y = label)

frame = \(w) {
	map = abs |>
		mutate(cases = cut(incidence_w[w, ], CASES_AT, include.lowest = TRUE,
			dig.lab = 5)) |>
		ggplot() +
		geom_sf(aes(fill = cases), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.05,
			show.legend = TRUE) +
		scale_fill_brewer(palette = "YlOrRd", drop = FALSE) +
		labs(fill = "Cases per\n100,000") +
		theme_void()
	cases_week = series(regional, "inc", w, "Cases per 100,000\nin Catalunya") +
		theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())
	trips_week = series(mobility, "trips", w,
		"Trips out of ABS\n(millions a day)")
	map / cases_week / trips_week +
		plot_layout(heights = c(3, 1, 1)) +
		plot_annotation(title = paste("Catalunya, week of", day(dates[w])))
}
```

## Spatial clustering

Before fitting, we check whether incidence clusters in space, which is what a neighbour component assumes.

```{r}
#| label: fig-lisa
#| fig-cap: "Left: cumulative cases per 100,000 in each ABS against the mean of its neighbours. Grey lines mark the means. Middle and right: local Moran's I clusters (9,999 permutations, p < 0.05 after false discovery rate adjustment), with a zoom to the high-high cores."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.5
# Local Moran's I of cumulative incidence, row-standardised adjacency weights,
# 9,999 permutations, false discovery rate 5% (Pebesma and Bivand 2023, ch. 15)
cum = rowSums(Y) / popv * 1e5
lw = spdep::mat2listw((a > 0) * 1, style = "W")
local = spdep::localmoran_perm(cum, lw, nsim = 9999, iseed = 1)
cluster = spdep::hotspot(local, Prname = "Pr(z != E(Ii)) Sim", cutoff = 0.05,
	p.adjust = "fdr", droplevels = FALSE)
CLUSTER = c(`High-High` = "#b2182b", `Low-Low` = "#2166ac",
	`High-Low` = "#f4a582", `Low-High` = "#92c5de")

# Moran scatterplot: each ABS against the mean of its neighbours
scatter = data.frame(cum = cum, lag = spdep::lag.listw(lw, cum),
		cluster = cluster) |>
	ggplot(aes(cum, lag, colour = cluster)) +
	geom_vline(xintercept = mean(cum), colour = "grey60") +
	geom_hline(yintercept = mean(cum), colour = "grey60") +
	geom_point(size = 1.2) +
	scale_colour_manual(values = CLUSTER, na.value = "grey75", guide = "none") +
	labs(x = "Cases per 100,000 in the ABS",
		y = "Mean of its neighbours")

# Cluster map, for Catalunya and zoomed to the high-high cores
cluster_map = \(zoom = NULL) abs |>
	mutate(cluster = cluster) |>
	ggplot() +
	geom_sf(aes(fill = cluster), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.05,
		show.legend = TRUE) +
	coord_sf(xlim = zoom[c(1, 3)], ylim = zoom[c(2, 4)]) +
	scale_fill_manual(values = CLUSTER, na.value = "grey90",
		na.translate = TRUE, drop = FALSE,
		labels = \(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "Not significant", x)) +
	labs(fill = NULL) +
	theme_void()
high = abs[which(cluster == "High-High"), ] |>
	st_buffer(3000) |>
	st_bbox()
scatter + cluster_map() + cluster_map(high) +
	plot_layout(widths = c(1.2, 1, 0.7), guides = "collect") +
	plot_annotation(title = "Catalunya: local clusters of cumulative cases",
		subtitle = "Right: zoom to the high-high cores")
```

Cumulative incidence clusters between adjacent ABS: global Moran's I is
`r sprintf("%.2f", spdep::moran.test(cum, lw)$estimate[[1]])`. Local Moran's I [@pebesma2023] finds
`r sum(cluster == "High-High", na.rm = TRUE)` high-high and `r sum(cluster == "Low-Low", na.rm = TRUE)` low-low
cores, ABS whose incidence and that of their neighbours are both above or both below the mean. The high-high cores
are `r paste(abs$name[which(cluster == "High-High")], collapse = ", ")`. The low-low cores lie mostly along the
southern coast, from the Penedès and the Garraf to the Ebre delta.

# Neighbourhoods

The three models differ only in the neighbour weights $w_{ji}$. The weights split the cases of each source ABS $j$
across the ABS $i$ it is linked to, so the weights from each source sum to 1.

| Version | How the weights fall | Question it answers |
|---|---|---|
| Boundaries | With the number of borders crossed, at an estimated rate | Does adjacency describe how cases spread between ABS? |
| Trip orders | With the rank of each destination by trips, in rings of the same size as by boundaries, at an estimated rate | Are the ABS people travel to most better neighbours than the adjacent ones? |
| Trip shares | In proportion to the share of trips to each destination, with no rate to estimate | Does the volume of trips describe spread between ABS without a distance rule? |

- **Boundaries**: ABS that touch at a single point count as sharing a border (queen adjacency).
- **Trip orders**: each ABS's destinations are ranked by their mean daily trips over the whole period. The
  destinations with most trips take order 1, the next take order 2 and then order 3, with as many ABS at each order
  as by boundaries. Only which ABS count as close changes, which makes the comparison with boundaries a fair test of who
  the neighbours are.
- **Trip shares**: if 10% of the trips leaving ABS $j$ end in ABS $i$, then 10% of $j$'s neighbour weight goes to $i$.
  Every ABS that receives trips from $j$ is a neighbour.

## Create neighbourhoods

```{r}
#| label: neighbourhoods
# Boundary order, [from, to]
geo = nbOrder((a > 0) * 1, maxlag = Inf)
dimnames(geo) = list(ids, ids)

# Number of ABS at each boundary order by origin, orders above 3 as 4
size = geo |>
	apply(1, \(o) tabulate(pmin(o[o > 0], 4), 4)) |>
	t()
stopifnot(rowSums(size) == n - 1)

# Trip order, [from, to]
mob = matrix(0L, n, n, dimnames = list(ids, ids))
for (j in 1:n) {
	rank = order(trips[j, -j], decreasing = TRUE)
	mob[j, -j][rank] = rep(1:4, size[j, ])
}
stopifnot(rowSums(mob == 1) == rowSums(geo == 1))


# Trip shares, [from, to], each row sums to 1
share = trips / rowSums(trips)
stopifnot(all.equal(unname(rowSums(share)), rep(1, n)))
```

## Stability of trip orders across restriction phases

The restrictions split the period into phases, runs of days with the same measures in force. Trip orders built from
each phase's trips show whether people's destinations changed with the restrictions.

```{r}
#| label: phases
# Restriction phase of each day: the measures in force, in words
MEASURE = c(npi_alarm = "state of alarm",
	npi_hibernation = "non-essential work suspended", npi_curfew = "curfew",
	npi_hospitality = "bars and restaurants closed")
days_npi = panel |>
	filter(id == ids[1]) |>
	arrange(date)
in_force = as.matrix(days_npi[names(MEASURE)]) == 1
phase_name = apply(in_force, 1, \(x) if (any(x)) paste(MEASURE[x],
	collapse = ", ") else "no restriction")
phases = unique(phase_name)
phase = match(phase_name, phases)

# Mean daily trips between ABS in each phase, [origin, destination, phase]
index = \(v) setNames(data.frame(ids, seq_len(n)), c(v, paste0(v, "_i")))
flows = spain("data/cat_od_bha_reprojected") |>
	arrow::open_dataset() |>
	inner_join(index("source"), by = "source") |>
	inner_join(index("target"), by = "target") |>
	inner_join(data.frame(date = d$dates, phase = phase), by = "date") |>
	group_by(source_i, target_i, phase) |>
	summarise(trips = sum(trips)) |>
	collect()
trips_phase = array(0, c(n, n, length(phases)))
trips_phase[cbind(flows$source_i, flows$target_i, flows$phase)] = flows$trips
trips_phase = sweep(trips_phase, 3, tabulate(phase), "/")

# Trip orders of each phase, and the share of neighbours they keep
trip_orders = \(x) {
	diag(x) = 0
	m = matrix(0L, n, n, dimnames = list(ids, ids))
	for (j in 1:n) {
		rank = order(x[j, -j], decreasing = TRUE)
		m[j, -j][rank] = rep(1:4, size[j, ])
	}
	m
}
same_order = \(x, y, k, rows = 1:n) mean(sapply(rows, \(j) {
	g = x[j, ] == k
	if (any(g)) mean(y[j, g] == k) else NA
}), na.rm = TRUE)
phase_orders = lapply(seq_along(phases), \(p) trip_orders(trips_phase[, , p]))
stability = data.frame(Phase = sub("^(.)", "\\U\\1", phases, perl = TRUE),
	Days = tabulate(phase),
	t(sapply(phase_orders, \(m) round(100 * sapply(1:3, same_order, x = mob,
		y = m)))))
names(stability)[3:5] = paste0("Order ", 1:3, " (%)")
knitr::kable(stability)
```

The table gives the share of an ABS's neighbours at each order that are the same in a phase as over the whole period.
An ABS's most-visited destinations hardly change: `r min(stability[[3]])`% to `r max(stability[[3]])`% of order-1
neighbours stay the same in every phase, the lowest when non-essential work was suspended. One matrix for the whole
period is therefore a fair summary, and weights that switch with the phase do not improve the fit (Section 5.1.2).

## Urban and rural ABS

```{r}
#| label: urban-rural
# Population density terciles
area = read.csv(spain("outputs/catalunya/tables/cat_abs_areas.csv"),
	colClasses = c(id = "character"))
density = popv / area$area_km2[match(ids, area$id)]
setting = cut(density, quantile(density, 0:3 / 3), include.lowest = TRUE,
	labels = c("Rural", "Middle", "Urban"))

# Trip neighbours that are also boundary neighbours, and the trips they take
order1_trips = sapply(1:n, \(j) sum(trips[j, mob[j, ] == 1]) / sum(trips[j, ]))
urban_rural = data.frame(Setting = levels(setting),
		`People per km² (median)` = round(tapply(density, setting, median)),
		`Order-1 trip neighbours also adjacent (%)` = sapply(levels(setting),
			\(s) round(100 * same_order(mob, geo, 1, which(setting == s)))),
		`Trips to order-1 trip neighbours (%)` = round(100 *
			tapply(order1_trips, setting, mean)), check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(urban_rural, row.names = FALSE)
```

Boundaries and trips disagree most in urban ABS. Rural ABS send most of their trips to a few destinations, mostly
adjacent ones. Urban ABS spread their trips over many destinations, and fewer of their closest trip neighbours share a
border with them.

## Overlap of boundary and trip orders

```{r}
#| label: overlap
# Share of an ABS's boundary neighbours at order k that are trip neighbours
same = \(j, k) {
	g = geo[j, ] == k
	if (any(g)) sum(g & mob[j, ] == k) / sum(g) else NA
}
overlap = sapply(1:3, \(k) mean(sapply(1:n, same, k = k), na.rm = TRUE))
data.frame(Order = 1:3, `Same neighbours (%)` = round(100 * overlap),
		check.names = FALSE) |>
	knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-orders
#| fig-cap: "Order-1 to order-3 neighbours of the largest and the smallest ABS, by boundaries and by trip orders. Darker: higher order."
#| fig-height: 9
# Orders 1 to 3 around the largest and the smallest ABS
pick = c(`Largest ABS` = ids[which.max(popv)],
	`Smallest ABS` = ids[which.min(popv)])
ring = \(o, j) factor(ifelse(ids == j, "Origin", ifelse(o <= 3, o, NA)),
	names(ORDER))

# One row per origin: orders by boundaries and by trips, zoomed alike
map_orders = \(label, j) {
	x = bind_rows(
		mutate(abs, by = "By boundaries", order = ring(geo[j, ], j)),
		mutate(abs, by = "By trip orders", order = ring(mob[j, ], j)))
	zoom = x |>
		filter(!is.na(order)) |>
		st_bbox()
	ggplot(x) +
		geom_sf(aes(fill = order), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
		geom_sf_text(data = filter(x, order %in% 1:3),
			aes(label = order, colour = order == 3), size = 2.5,
			check_overlap = TRUE) +
		facet_wrap(~by) +
		coord_sf(datum = st_crs(4326), xlim = zoom[c(1, 3)],
			ylim = zoom[c(2, 4)]) +
		scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 3) +
		scale_fill_manual(values = ORDER, na.value = "grey92",
			na.translate = FALSE, drop = FALSE) +
		scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "black"),
			guide = "none") +
		labs(subtitle = paste0(label, ": ", abs$name[abs$id == j]),
			x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Order")
}
Map(map_orders, names(pick), pick) |>
	wrap_plots(ncol = 1, guides = "collect") +
	plot_annotation(title = "Catalunya: neighbour orders 1 to 3")
```

# Model

The model for the cases $Y_{it}$ in ABS $i$ in week $t$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
Y_{it} \mid Y_{\cdot,\,t-1} &\sim \operatorname{NegBin}(\mu_{it},\ \psi), \quad \operatorname{Var} = \mu_{it}(1 + \psi\,\mu_{it}) \\[4pt]
\mu_{it} &= \underbrace{e_i\,\nu_t}_{\text{endemic}}
	+ \underbrace{\lambda\,Y_{i,t-1}}_{\text{autoregressive}}
	+ \underbrace{\phi_i \sum_{j \ne i} w_{ji}\,Y_{j,t-1}}_{\text{neighbour}} \\[4pt]
e_i &= \text{population share of ABS } i \\[4pt]
\log \nu_t &= \alpha_\nu + \beta \underbrace{t}_{0 \text{ in week 1}} \\[4pt]
\log \phi_i &= \alpha_\phi + \tau \underbrace{\log N_i}_{N_i = \text{population of ABS } i \text{, centred}} \\[4pt]
w_{ji} &= \frac{o_{ji}^{-d}}{\sum_{k:\, o_{jk} \le 3} o_{jk}^{-d}} \text{ for } \underbrace{o_{ji}}_{\text{order of } i \text{ from } j} \le 3,
	\text{ and 0 beyond} \quad \text{(boundaries, trip orders)} \\[4pt]
w_{ji} &= \frac{F_{ji}}{\sum_{k \ne j} F_{jk}}, \quad \underbrace{F_{ji}}_{\text{mean daily trips from } j \text{ to } i} \quad \text{(trip shares)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The power-law weights follow @meyer2014, with neighbours up to order 3: beyond it, the weight of each ABS pair is
small. The parameters are estimated by maximum likelihood [@meyer2017]. The first
week only provides the lagged cases, so the models are fitted to weeks 2 to 58.

## Covariates

Each model is also fitted with temperature and restrictions in the autoregressive and neighbour components:

$$
\log \lambda_{it} = \alpha_\lambda + \boldsymbol{\gamma}^\top \mathbf{x}_{it}, \qquad
\log \phi_{it} = \alpha_\phi + \tau \log N_i + \boldsymbol{\delta}^\top \mathbf{x}_{it}
$$

The covariates $\mathbf{x}_{it}$ are weekly values:

- **Temperature**: the mean daily temperature in the ABS, centred and per 5 °C.
- **State of alarm**, **non-essential work suspended** and **bars and restaurants closed**: the share of days in the
  week with the measure in force.

The curfew is left out: in Catalunya it ran on the same days as the second state of alarm. The effects
$e^{\gamma}$ and $e^{\delta}$ are rate ratios. For temperature, they compare weeks 5 °C apart. For a restriction,
they compare a week with the measure in force on all seven days with a week without it. They describe associations
with the weekly cases, not the effect of a measure, and they act on the cases that follow from past cases, not on
trips.

## Model fitting

```{r}
#| label: fit
# Population matrix, [week, ABS]
pop = matrix(popv, 58, n, byrow = TRUE, dimnames = list(NULL, ids))

# One sts object for each neighbourhood
make_sts = \(nb) sts(observed = t(Y), start = c(2020, 13), frequency = 52,
	population = pop / sum(popv), neighbourhood = nb)
sts_geo = make_sts(geo)
sts_mob = make_sts(mob)

# Shared model, with the neighbour weights set for each version
model = list(
	end = list(f = ~1 + t, offset = population(sts_geo)),
	ar = list(f = ~1),
	ne = list(f = ~1 + logpop, weights = W_powerlaw(maxlag = 3)),
	family = "NegBin1",
	data = list(logpop = log(pop) - mean(log(popv))),
	subset = 2:58)
shares_model = modifyList(model, list(ne = list(weights = share)))

# Fit all three
fits = list(
	Boundaries = hhh4(sts_geo, model),
	`Trip orders` = hhh4(sts_mob, model),
	`Trip shares` = hhh4(sts_geo, shares_model))
stopifnot(sapply(fits, \(f) f$convergence),
	lengths(lapply(fits, coef)) == c(7, 7, 6))
```

```{r}
#| label: covariates
# Weekly covariates, [week, ABS]
covariates = list(
	temp = (weekly("temp_mean") - mean(weekly("temp_mean"))) / 5,
	alarm = weekly("npi_alarm"),
	work = weekly("npi_hibernation"),
	bars = weekly("npi_hospitality"))
stopifnot(all(sapply(covariates, dim) == c(58, n)))

# Same three models with the covariates in both epidemic components
with_covariates = \(m) modifyList(m, list(
	ar = list(f = ~1 + temp + alarm + work + bars),
	ne = list(f = ~1 + logpop + temp + alarm + work + bars),
	data = c(m$data, covariates)))
fits_cov = list(
	Boundaries = hhh4(sts_geo, with_covariates(model)),
	`Trip orders` = hhh4(sts_mob, with_covariates(model)),
	`Trip shares` = hhh4(sts_geo, with_covariates(shares_model)))
stopifnot(sapply(fits_cov, \(f) f$convergence))
```

# Results

## Which neighbourhood fits best

### In-sample fit

AIC weighs how well a model fits against how many parameters it uses: lower is better, and a difference of more
than about 10 is clear. The two power-law models have seven parameters and the trip-share model six.

```{r}
#| label: comparison
# Compare
cmp = fits |>
	sapply(diagnostics) |>
	t()
best = names(fits)[which.min(cmp[, "AIC"])]

# The conclusions below are written for boundaries fitting best
stopifnot(best == "Boundaries")
cmp |>
	as.data.frame() |>
	mutate(Model = rownames(cmp), .before = 1) |>
	mutate(`AIC - best` = AIC - min(AIC), .after = AIC) |>
	arrange(AIC) |>
	knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 2), row.names = FALSE)
```

### Trip neighbours by restriction phase

Weights that switch with the restriction phase of each week, against one matrix for the whole period. For trip
orders, the decay is profiled over a grid and counted as one parameter.

```{r}
#| label: phase-fits
# Phase of each week: the phase of most of its days
week_phase = sapply(split(phase, week),
	\(p) as.integer(names(which.max(table(p)))))
by_week = \(f) {
	x = array(0, c(n, n, 58))
	for (w in 1:58) x[, , w] = f(week_phase[w])
	x
}
fit_weights = \(W) hhh4(sts_geo,
	modifyList(model, list(ne = list(weights = W))))
row_norm = \(m) m / rowSums(m)
powerlaw = \(o, dd) row_norm(ifelse(o >= 1 & o <= 3, pmax(o, 1)^-dd, 0))

# Trip shares by phase
shares_phase = by_week(\(p) row_norm(`diag<-`(trips_phase[, , p], 0))) |>
	fit_weights()

# Trip orders by phase, decay profiled
grid = seq(0.4, 3, by = 0.1)
profile = sapply(grid, \(dd) {
	P = lapply(phase_orders, powerlaw, dd = dd)
	as.numeric(logLik(fit_weights(by_week(\(p) P[[p]]))))
})
data.frame(Neighbours = c("Trip shares", "Trip orders"),
		`One matrix` = sapply(fits[c("Trip shares", "Trip orders")], AIC),
		`By phase` = c(AIC(shares_phase), -2 * max(profile) + 2 * 7),
		check.names = FALSE) |>
	knitr::kable(digits = 0, row.names = FALSE)
```

### One-week-ahead forecasts

Each of the last 20 weeks is forecast from a refit to the weeks before it [@meyer2014]. Lower scores are better.
The permutation test compares each trip model's logarithmic scores with those of the boundary model.

```{r}
#| label: osa
# Fit to week tp, predict week tp + 1, for the last 20 weeks
osa = lapply(fits, oneStepAhead, tp = c(38, 57), type = "rolling",
	which.start = "final", verbose = FALSE)
sc = lapply(osa, scores, which = c("logs", "rps", "dss"), individual = TRUE,
	reverse = FALSE)
stopifnot(sapply(sc, \(s) dim(s)[1]) == 20)

# Permutation tests of the logarithmic scores against boundaries
p_logs = sapply(names(fits)[-1], \(k) permutationTest(sc[[k]][, , "logs"],
	sc$Boundaries[, , "logs"], nPermutation = 999, verbose = FALSE)$pVal.permut)

# Mean scores
sc |>
	sapply(\(s) colMeans(s, dims = 2)) |>
	t() |>
	as.data.frame() |>
	mutate(p = c("", sprintf("%.3f", p_logs))) |>
	knitr::kable(digits = 4, col.names = c("Logarithmic",
		"Ranked probability", "Dawid-Sebastiani", "p (logarithmic)"))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-predictions
#| fig-cap: "Weekly cases in Catalunya over the last 20 weeks: observed (points) and one-week-ahead forecast mean (line). Band: 95% interval for the count variation alone."
#| fig-height: 7
# Weekly cases in Catalunya: predicted mean and 95% interval from 2,000 draws
set.seed(1)
interval = \(o) {
	draws = sapply(seq_len(nrow(o$pred)), \(w) colSums(matrix(rnbinom(n * 2000,
		mu = o$pred[w, ], size = exp(o$psi[w, 1])), n)))
	data.frame(date = dates[as.integer(rownames(o$pred))],
		mean = rowSums(o$pred), lo = apply(draws, 2, quantile, 0.025),
		hi = apply(draws, 2, quantile, 0.975), observed = rowSums(o$observed))
}
predictions = osa |>
	lapply(interval) |>
	bind_rows(.id = "model")

# Lag of the boundary model's predictions around the observed peak
lag = predictions |>
	filter(model == "Boundaries") |>
	mutate(after = date > date[which.max(observed)])
peak_obs = lag[which.max(lag$observed), ]
peak_pred = lag[which.max(lag$mean), ]
lag_weeks = as.integer(peak_pred$date - peak_obs$date) / 7
rise = filter(lag, date < peak_obs$date)
fall = filter(lag, after)
below = c(sum(rise$mean < rise$observed), nrow(rise))
above = c(sum(fall$mean > fall$observed), nrow(fall))

# Predicted against observed, one panel per model
predictions |>
	ggplot(aes(date)) +
	geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi, fill = model), alpha = 0.3) +
	geom_line(aes(y = mean, colour = model)) +
	geom_point(aes(y = observed, shape = "Observed cases"), size = 1.2) +
	facet_wrap(~model, ncol = 1) +
	scale_colour_manual(values = MODEL, aesthetics = c("colour", "fill"),
		guide = "none") +
	scale_shape_manual(values = 16) +
	labs(title = "Catalunya: one-week-ahead forecasts of weekly cases",
		x = NULL, y = "Cases a week", shape = NULL) +
	theme(legend.position = "top")
```

All three models react to the turning point of the winter wave a week late. Cases peaked at
`r format(round(peak_obs$observed), big.mark = ",")` in the week of `r day(peak_obs$date)`, and the boundary model's
forecasts peaked `r lag_weeks` week`r if (lag_weeks != 1) "s"` later, at `r format(round(peak_pred$mean), big.mark = ",")`.
The forecasts run below the observed cases in `r below[1]` of `r below[2]` weeks before the peak and above them in
`r above[1]` of `r above[2]` weeks after it, as each week is forecast largely from the week before.

As regional totals, the three forecasts are almost the same: the neighbourhood matters for where cases occur rather
than for how many. The band leaves out parameter uncertainty and the correlation between ABS, so it is narrower
than the full uncertainty.

## Parameters and neighbour weights

Estimates with 95% Wald intervals, computed on the log scale for the rates, the trend and ψ.

```{r}
#| label: parameters
# Coefficients reported as exp(estimate)
EXP = c("ar.1", "ne.1", "end.1", "end.t")
LABEL = c(ar.1 = "Autoregressive rate λ",
	ne.1 = "Neighbour rate φ, ABS of geometric-mean population, exp(α_φ)",
	ne.logpop = "Population exponent τ",
	end.1 = "Endemic cases a week, all ABS, week 1, exp(α_ν)",
	end.t = "Endemic trend per week, exp(β)",
	neweights.d = "Decay d",
	overdisp = "Overdispersion ψ")

# Estimate (95% interval) by coefficient name, and the dominant eigenvalue
estimates = \(f) {
	x = wald(f, EXP)
	x = setNames(sprintf("%.3f (%.3f to %.3f)", x[, 1], x[, 2], x[, 3]),
		rownames(x))
	c(x[names(LABEL)], `Dominant eigenvalue` = sprintf("%.2f", getMaxEV(f)[1]))
}
table = sapply(fits, estimates)
table[is.na(table)] = ""
rownames(table) = c(LABEL, "Dominant eigenvalue")
knitr::kable(table)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-decay
#| fig-cap: "Fitted weight of every ABS pair by order. Each ABS's weights sum to 1. Trip shares are grouped by trip order."
#| fig-height: 4
# Decay of the two power-law models
decay = fits[c("Boundaries", "Trip orders")] |>
	sapply(\(f) coef(f, se = TRUE)["neweights.d", ]) |>
	t()

# Fitted weight of every ABS pair by order, trip shares by trip order
weights = Map(\(f, o) data.frame(order = c(o), w = c(getNEweights(f))),
		fits, list(geo, mob, mob)) |>
	bind_rows(.id = "model") |>
	filter(order > 0) |>
	mutate(order = factor(pmin(order, 4), 1:4, c(1:3, "4+")))

# Mean share of each ABS's outgoing weight on its order-1 neighbours
w1 = Map(\(f, o) mean(rowSums(getNEweights(f) * (o == 1))), fits,
	list(geo, mob, mob)) |>
	unlist()

# Weights by order, one box per model
weights |>
	ggplot(aes(order, w, fill = model)) +
	geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.2, linewidth = 0.3) +
	scale_fill_manual(values = MODEL, labels = c(sprintf("%s (d = %.2f)",
		rownames(decay), decay[, 1]), "Trip shares (by trip order)")) +
	labs(title = "Catalunya: fitted neighbour weights by order",
		x = "Order", y = "Weight", fill = NULL) +
	theme(legend.position = "inside", legend.position.inside = c(0.98, 0.95),
		legend.justification.inside = c(1, 1))
```

On average, order-1 neighbours receive `r round(100 * w1[["Boundaries"]])`% of an ABS's neighbour weight by
boundaries and `r round(100 * w1[["Trip orders"]])`% by trip orders. With trip shares, the same number of top
destinations receive `r round(100 * w1[["Trip shares"]])`%. The neighbour component works mainly through the few ABS
closest by each definition.

## How the fitted cases split

### Over time

```{r}
#| label: fig-time
#| fig-cap: "Fitted weekly cases in Catalunya by component, with the observed cases and each component's share of all fitted cases."
#| fig-height: 8
# Share of all fitted cases by component
cs = lapply(fits, components)
shares = cs |>
	sapply(\(m) 100 * sapply(m[names(COMPONENT)], sum) / sum(m$mean)) |>
	t()

# Observed cases and the share labels
observed_total = data.frame(date = dates, cases = colSums(Y))
share_label = data.frame(model = rownames(shares), date = dates[1],
	label = sprintf(paste0("Share of fitted cases\nEndemic %.1f%%\n",
		"Autoregressive %.1f%%\nNeighbour %.1f%%"),
		shares[, "Endemic"], shares[, "Autoregressive"],
		shares[, "Neighbour"]))

# Fitted weekly cases by component, one panel per model
cs |>
	lapply(long) |>
	bind_rows(.id = "model") |>
	summarise(cases = sum(cases), .by = c(model, date, component)) |>
	ggplot(aes(date, cases)) +
	geom_area(aes(fill = component)) +
	geom_point(data = observed_total, aes(shape = "Observed cases"),
		size = 0.5) +

	scale_shape_manual(values = 16) +

		x = NULL, y = "Cases a week", fill = NULL, shape = NULL) +
	theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## Temperature and restrictions

```{r}
#| label: covariate-aic
# AIC with and without covariates
gain = sapply(fits, AIC) - sapply(fits_cov, AIC)
best_cov = names(fits_cov)[which.min(sapply(fits_cov, AIC))]
data.frame(Model = names(fits), `AIC without` = sapply(fits, AIC),
		`AIC with covariates` = sapply(fits_cov, AIC), check.names = FALSE) |>
	mutate(`AIC with - best` = `AIC with covariates` -
		min(`AIC with covariates`)) |>
	knitr::kable(digits = 0, row.names = FALSE)
```


```{r}
#| label: covariate-effects
# Rate ratios with 95% intervals, by component and model
COVARIATE = c(temp = "Temperature (per 5 °C)", alarm = "State of alarm",
	work = "Non-essential work suspended", bars = "Bars and restaurants closed")
rows = paste0(rep(c("ar.", "ne."), each = 4), names(COVARIATE))
rate_ratios = \(f) {
	x = wald(f, rows)[rows, ]
	setNames(sprintf("%.2f (%.2f to %.2f)", x[, 1], x[, 2], x[, 3]), rows)
}
# One association in words, for the boundary model
say = \(r, rate) {
	x = wald(fits_cov$Boundaries, rows)[r, ]
	ci = sprintf("(%.2f, %.2f to %.2f)", x[1], x[2], x[3])
	if (x[2] <= 1 && x[3] >= 1) paste(rate, "no clear change", ci)
	else sprintf("%s %d%% %s %s", rate, round(100 * abs(1 - x[1])),
		if (x[1] < 1) "lower" else "higher", ci)
}
fits_cov |>
	sapply(\(f) rate_ratios(f)[rows]) |>
	`rownames<-`(paste0(rep(c("Autoregressive λ: ", "Neighbour φ: "),
		each = 4), COVARIATE)) |>
	knitr::kable()
```

Rate ratios in the boundary model, with 95% intervals:

- **Temperature, 5 °C warmer**: `r say("ar.temp", "λ")`, `r say("ne.temp", "φ")`.
- **State of alarm**: `r say("ar.alarm", "λ")`, `r say("ne.alarm", "φ")`.
- **Non-essential work suspended**: `r say("ar.work", "λ")`, `r say("ne.work", "φ")`.
- **Bars and restaurants closed**: `r say("ar.bars", "λ")`, `r say("ne.bars", "φ")`.

The suspension of non-essential work lasted 11 days, inside the first state of alarm, so its estimates rest on two
weeks and are uncertain.

# Conclusions

## In plain words

- **Cases cluster.** Areas with many cases tend to sit next to other areas with many cases, so cases in one area
  help predict cases in the areas around it.
- **Shared borders work best.** Defining an area's neighbours by the areas it borders explains and forecasts the
  weekly cases better than defining them by where its residents travel.
- **Most new cases follow earlier cases in the same area.** In the boundary model, about
  `r round(shares["Boundaries", "Autoregressive"])`% of the fitted cases are linked to past cases in the same area,
  `r round(shares["Boundaries", "Neighbour"])`% to past cases in neighbouring areas and the rest to neither.
- **Where people go hardly changed with the restrictions.** Even under lockdown, `r min(stability[[3]])`% to
  `r max(stability[[3]])`% of each area's most-visited places stayed the same, so one travel network describes the
  whole period.
- **Cities differ.** City residents spread their trips over many places, not mainly next door, so the border and
  travel definitions disagree most in cities.
- **Restrictions and warm weather went with slower spread.** A week fully under a state of alarm had about
  `r round(100 * (1 - wald(fits_cov$Boundaries, rows)["ar.alarm", 1]))`% fewer new cases per earlier case in the same
  area, and a week 5 °C warmer about `r round(100 * (1 - wald(fits_cov$Boundaries, rows)["ar.temp", 1]))`% fewer.
  These are associations, not measured effects of the measures.

## In detail

1. **`r best` fit best.** AIC is `r round(cmp["Trip orders", "AIC"] - cmp["Boundaries", "AIC"])` higher with trip
   orders and `r round(cmp["Trip shares", "AIC"] - cmp["Boundaries", "AIC"])` higher with trip shares. The
   one-week-ahead logarithmic score is `r sprintf("%.3f", mean(sc$Boundaries[, , "logs"]))` with boundaries,
   against `r sprintf("%.3f", mean(sc[["Trip orders"]][, , "logs"]))` with trip orders (p =
   `r sprintf("%.3f", p_logs[["Trip orders"]])`) and `r sprintf("%.3f", mean(sc[["Trip shares"]][, , "logs"]))`
   with trip shares (p = `r sprintf("%.3f", p_logs[["Trip shares"]])`).
2. **Boundary and trip orders overlap only partly.** On average, `r round(100 * overlap[1])`% of an ABS's order-1
   neighbours are the same in both. This falls to `r round(100 * overlap[3])`% at order 3.
3. **Neighbour weights fall with order.** The decay d is
   `r sprintf("%.2f", decay["Boundaries", 1])` with boundaries and `r sprintf("%.2f", decay["Trip orders", 1])` with
   trip orders. At these values, an order-2 neighbour gets
   `r round(100 * 2^-decay["Boundaries", 1])`% of the weight of an order-1 neighbour with boundaries and
   `r round(100 * 2^-decay["Trip orders", 1])`% with trip orders.
4. **The neighbour rate φ grows most with population with `r tolower(names(which.max(sapply(fits, \(f) coef(f)[["ne.logpop"]]))))`.**
   The population exponent τ is
   `r sprintf("%.2f", coef(fits$Boundaries)[["ne.logpop"]])` with boundaries,
   `r sprintf("%.2f", coef(fits[["Trip orders"]])[["ne.logpop"]])` with trip orders and
   `r sprintf("%.2f", coef(fits[["Trip shares"]])[["ne.logpop"]])` with trip shares.
5. **The neighbour share depends on the neighbourhood.** It is `r round(shares["Boundaries", "Neighbour"], 1)`% with
   boundaries, `r round(shares["Trip orders", "Neighbour"], 1)`% with trip orders and
   `r round(shares["Trip shares", "Neighbour"], 1)`% with trip shares. Where it is lower, the autoregressive and
   endemic components take a larger share.
6. **Temperature and restrictions `r if (all(gain > 0)) "improve every model" else "do not improve every model"`.**
   AIC falls by `r knitr::combine_words(format(round(gain), big.mark = ","), oxford_comma = FALSE)` for boundaries, trip orders and
   trip shares. With
   covariates, `r tolower(best_cov)` `r if (best_cov == best) "still fit best" else "fit best"`.
7. **Trip neighbours hardly change across restriction phases.** `r min(stability[[3]])`% to
   `r max(stability[[3]])`% of order-1 trip neighbours stay the same in every phase, and weights that switch with the
   phase fit worse than one matrix.
8. **Boundaries and trips disagree most in urban ABS.** `r urban_rural[3, 3]`% of an urban ABS's order-1 trip
   neighbours are adjacent, against `r urban_rural[1, 3]`% of a rural ABS's, and they take `r urban_rural[3, 4]`% of
   its trips, against `r urban_rural[1, 4]`%.

# Next steps

None of the models has a mobility term: trips enter only through the neighbourhood. The next step keeps neighbours
by boundaries and adds trips as a fourth component, mobility. This separates cases linked to past cases in adjacent
ABS from cases linked to past cases in ABS connected by travel [@slater2025]. `hhh4` has only three components, so
we will compare two extensions:

- **Mixed neighbour weights**: a single neighbour component whose weights combine boundaries and trips, with the
  mixing proportion estimated from the data.
- **A separate mobility component**: a fourth term with its own rate and weights from trips. `hhh4` cannot fit
  such a term, so this option needs other software.

Only the second gives mobility its own share of the fitted cases.
